title: Open-Label Study of TX000045 in Participants With Pulmonary Hypertension due to Interstitial Lung Disease
official: An Open-Label Study to Assess the Hemodynamic Effect and the Safety of TX000045 After 16 Weeks of Treatment in Participants With Pulmonary Hypertension due to Interstitial Lung Disease
summary:
Main objective: 1.To assess the effect of TX000045 on pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) in participants with PH-ILD.
2.To assess the safety and tolerability of TX000045 in participants with PH-ILD.
conditions: Pulmonary hypertension secondary to interstitial lung disease
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Participants are eligible to be included in the study only if all the following criteria apply: 1. Adults aged 18-80 years, inclusive
2. 2. For people of childbearing potential (POCBP) and male participants with partners of childbearing potential, the participant must be willing to use at least one highly effective form of contraception. A highly effective method of contraception is one that has a failure rate of <1% when used consistently and correctly
3. 3. Confirmed diagnosis of ILD based on imaging: chest CT performed within the past 12 months with fibrotic lung disease consistent with idiopathic interstitial pneumonia, ILD in association with connective tissue disease, occupational ILD, or chronic HP. Chest CTs will be centrally read for eligibility.
4. 4. 40% predicted ≤ FVC ≤ 80% predicted at screening.
5. 5. At least ONE of the following is required to undergo the first screening visit:  a) Documented diagnostic RHC within 18 months of screening with mPAP ≥25 mm Hg, pulmonary capillary wedge pressure ≤15 mm Hg, and PVR ≥4 Wood units. b) Documented ECHO within 18 months of screening with RV (or pulmonary artery) systolic pressure >46 mm Hg or TAPSE/SPAP ≤0.38 and absence of clinically significant left ventricular dysfunction as assessed by the investigator.
6. 6. On the screening RHC within 21 days of Day 1, mPAP ≥25 mm Hg, PCWP ≤15 mm Hg, and PVR ≥4 Wood units. Participants with 12 < PCWP ≤ 15 may be enrolled only with permission of the sponsor or CRO medical monitor.
7. 7. Classified as NYHA Class II or III in the assessment of the investigator.
8. 8. 6MWD > 150m and < 450m at each of the 2 screening visits
9. 9. Able to adhere to the study visit schedule, understand and comply with all protocol requirements, and provide written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Participants are excluded from the study if any of the following criteria apply:  1. Has a confirmed or suspected diagnosis of pulmonary hypertension in WHO Group 1, WHO Group 2, WHO Group 4, or WHO Group 5.
2. 10. Has HIV seropositivity at the first screening visit.
3. 11. Has any of the clinical laboratory values at or relative to the first screening visit described in the study protocol.
4. 12. Has a history of severe allergic or anaphylactic reaction or hypersensitivity to recombinant proteins or excipients in the investigational product.
5. 13. History of or anticipated transplant of any organ.
6. 14. Initiated a new exercise program or intensified an exercise regimen within 3 months of the first screening visit or anticipates doing so during the study period.
7. 15. Is pregnant or breastfeeding
8. 16. History of active malignancy within 5 years before the first screening visit except for fully excised or treated basal cell carcinoma, cervical carcinoma in situ, or ≤2 squamous cell carcinomas of the skin.
9. 17. Life expectancy <12 months in the opinion of the investigator.
10. 18. Body mass index <18 kg/m2 or ≥45 kg/m2
11. 19. History of drug or alcohol abuse within the past 3 years or has a positive urine drug screen for prohibited drugs (marijuana use is permitted).
12. 2. Has received pulmonary medications as specified in the protocol
13. 20. Received any vaccination, including COVID-19 vaccination, within 1 week before dosing or plans to receive a vaccine during the study other than seasonal influenza or COVID-19 booster vaccination, which may be given between Weeks 6 and 12.
14. 21. Previously administered relaxin or relaxin fusion proteins including TX000045.
15. 22. Dosed in any clinical research study evaluating another investigational drug (including biologics) or therapy (including specific immunotherapy) within 90 days or ≤5 half-lives (whichever is longer) of an investigational biologic drug, or ≤4 weeks for other investigational products, before the first screening visit.
16. 23. Is mentally or legally incapacitated, has significant emotional problems at the time of the study, or has a history of significant psychiatric disorders at the discretion of the investigator.
17. 24. Has a history of any illness that, in the opinion of the investigator, might confound the results of the study or pose additional risk to the participant.
18. 25. Has any condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, significantly limits 6MWD, such as orthopedic injuries, arthritis, or angina.
19. 3. Has any of the pulmonary comorbidities described in the study protocol.
20. 4. Has any of the cardiovascular comorbidities described in the study protocol.
21. 5. Participants who are taking disease-modifying therapy for the underlying ILD (anti-fibrotics, immunosuppressives, and anti-inflammatory medications) who are not on stable doses for >30 days before the first screening visit or have initiated new ILD-directed therapies within 90 days before the first screening visit.
22. 6. Recently has taken inhaled medications as specified in the protocol
23. 7. Participants who are taking diuretics or using supplemental oxygen who are not on stable doses for >30 days before the first screening visit.
24. 8. Hospitalization for any reason or use of IV inotropes/vasopressors (eg, dobutamine, dopamine, norepinephrine, vasopressin) within 30 days before the first screening visit.
25. 9. Major surgery within 60 days of the first screening visit. Participants must have completely recovered from any previous surgery before the first screening visit.
